## Diffusion face coefficient at a wall: one-sided extrapolation instead of the ghost (automatic) {#sec-ch09-wallcoef}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** On an $x_1$ face that is a reflecting wall, takes the diffusion coefficient ($\rho$, $\rho c_v$,
or either times an $x_1$ profile) by linear extrapolation from the two nearest interior cells instead of
averaging the wall cell with its ghost.
**Switch.** None: automatic when the $x_1$ boundary function is named `reflecting_inner`/`_outer` or
`fixed_temperature_inner`/`_outer`. Every other face keeps the two-cell average.
**Order.** Second order at the wall face, against first order for the mirror average.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch09-wallcoef-extrap.
:::

A reflecting wall fills its ghost cells with the mirror image of the interior. That is the right state for the
Riemann solver, but the average of a cell and its mirror is the cell's own value, half a cell away from the wall,
so the face coefficient of a stratified column is off by a factor $e^{\mp h/2H}$ at the walls, an $O(h)$ error.
The diffusion module therefore extrapolates the coefficient from the two interior cells next to the wall, which
reads no ghost at all and is exact for a linear profile.

The fix is restricted to $x_1$ and to a whitelist of boundary names. An $x_2$ or $x_3$ reflecting face is as likely
to be a symmetry plane, where the mirror is exact and the average is the better estimate; and `reflecting` is the
default for every face a configuration does not name, so widening the rule would change runs that did not ask for
it. Periodic faces, outflow, custom and solid boundary functions keep the average.

*Aliases.* "Defect B" of `sources/canoe__diffusion_ghost_TECH_REPORT.md`; its "Defect A", the immersed-solid
placeholder state, is not fixed (Limits).

### Derivation

Let cell $0$ touch the wall and cell $1$ be its interior neighbour, with widths $h_0$, $h_1$. The wall face is
$h_0/2$ from the centre of cell $0$ and the two centres are $(h_0+h_1)/2$ apart, so the linear interpolant through the
two centre values, evaluated at the face, is

$$
q_f = (1+t)\,q_0 - t\,q_1, \qquad t = \frac{h_0}{h_0+h_1},
$$ {#eq-ch09-wallcoef-extrap}

the same expression at both walls, because the offset to the face and the direction to the second cell change sign
together. @eq-ch09-wallcoef-extrap is `extrapolate_to_wall` ([`diffusion.cpp:114-136`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L114-L136)). It is exact for
a linear $q$ on any widths [check `src/snapy_report/ch09/wallcoef_check.py`, output `wallcoef_check.out`, `[C1]`,
max error $8.9\times10^{-16}$ over 100 random stretched columns] and so second order for a smooth one. If
$q_f\le0$ the code returns $q_0$, which also reads no ghost (`[C3]`).

The mirror average, by contrast, returns $q_0$ itself. For $\rho=\rho_0e^{-x_1/H}$ with the lower wall at $x_1=0$
the ratio of the mirror average to the wall value is exactly $e^{-h/2H}$ at the lower wall and $e^{+h/2H}$ at the
upper one, an $O(h)$ error; the extrapolation error falls at second order (`[C2]`: fitted orders 0.994 and 1.985
for $h/H$ from $1/32$ to $1/64$).

Which fluxes the coefficient matters for follows from the mirror parities. Density and temperature are mirrored
even, so the face-normal temperature difference at a reflecting wall is exactly zero and the conductive wall flux
vanishes whatever the coefficient. The normal velocity is mirrored odd, so $\partial_1v_1 = 2v_{1,0}/h_0$ at the wall
(`[C4]`), and the viscous normal stress at the wall carries the coefficient. The fix changes the viscous wall flux
and, with an $x_1$ profile on conduction, nothing else at a reflecting wall.

*Exact and truncated.* The coefficient is exact for linear profiles and $O(h^2)$ otherwise; the normal-stress kernel
at the wall stays $O(h)$ (@sec-ch09-viscosity, Limits).

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-wallcoef-wall compares the two estimates at the lower wall.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-wallcoef-wall
#| fig-cap: "The diffusion coefficient at a reflecting $x_1$ wall (thick black line) for $\\rho=\\rho_0e^{-x_1/H}$ with $h=H/2$, shown as $\\rho/\\rho_0$ against $x_1/H$ (both dimensionless). The blue curve is the exact profile, the sky-blue circles the two interior cell values and the hatched reddish-purple cell the mirror ghost (reddish-purple circle). Their average is the vermillion square on the wall, which equals the wall cell's value; the bluish-green dashed line is the extrapolation from the two interior cells, which lands on the bluish-green diamond near the exact wall value."
#| fig-alt: "Plot of an exponential density near a wall, with a hatched ghost cell to the left of the wall, two interior cell values, the mirror-average point on the wall below the curve and the extrapolated point on the wall close to the curve."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.fig_wallcoef_wall import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The extrapolation is applied to the first and last $x_1$ face of a block when that face is a whitelisted wall and
the block has at least three $x_1$ faces (two interior cells); with fewer the average is kept, in
`face_coefficient` ([`diffusion.cpp:142-159`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L142-L159)). A seam between two blocks has no boundary function and so is never a wall.
The same rule applies to the product of a coefficient and an $x_1$ profile, which is extrapolated as one quantity
(@sec-ch09-x1profile). It runs wherever the module computes a coefficient, in every stage.

1. For each active direction `DiffusionImpl::forward` asks `is_wall_boundary` for the lower and upper $x_1$ face
   only ([`diffusion.cpp:496-502`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L496-L502)).
2. `is_wall_boundary` returns true for an installed function whose recorded name is on the whitelist
   ([`meshblock_options.cpp:243-272`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp#L243-L272)); a function with no recorded name warns once with `TORCH_WARN_ONCE` and returns false
   ([`meshblock_options.cpp:250-258`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp#L250-L258)).
3. `face_coefficient` averages every face and overwrites the wall faces with `extrapolate_to_wall`
   ([`diffusion.cpp:142-159`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L142-L159), [`diffusion.cpp:114-136`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L114-L136)).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Without a `boundary-condition.external` block no boundary functions exist and the rule never fires. Immersed
solids are read as fluid by the diffusion module, with a face heat capacity about 500 times too large.
:::

1. **Immersed solids (not fixed).** The solid placeholder state, $\rho=10^3$ and $p=10^9$ by default, is written into $\mathbf W$ by `mark_prim_solid_` before the forcings run
   ([`hydro_forward.cpp:217-218`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L217-L218)). A fluid face next to a solid
   then has $\rho c_v$ $500.5$ times the fluid value and a temperature jump of a factor 10 (`[C5]`). The source
   measured $+1.126125\times10^3$ of energy per stage in the two flanking cells of a uniform column
   [`sources/canoe__diffusion_ghost_TECH_REPORT.md` §3; sha
   snapy@43e04fda904d7401f1ee204c73b34460f09ff5fe, not a pin of this report]. No configuration in the tree combines
   a solid mask with diffusion; the path is deliberately left as it was (same report §3a). Not tested at the pin.
2. **Dormant without named boundaries.** No boundary block, or a function installed from Python with no `name`,
   means no wall: the average is used, with a one-time warning in the second case.
3. **`fixed_temperature_*`** is on the whitelist but no such boundary function is registered in the tree
   (chengcli/snapy#216), so that entry changes nothing at the pin.
4. **Positivity fallback** is element-wise and silent; a wall face can be second order in some columns and first
   order in others. Not observed to fire; not measured.
5. **Block too short.** With fewer than two interior $x_1$ cells, `nface` $<3$, the average is kept
   ([`diffusion.cpp:147-148`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/diffusion.cpp#L147-L148)).
